framework: Next Generation Science Standards — Engineering Design performance expectations (ETS1)

documents.title: NGSS Engineering Design: K-2-ETS1, 3-5-ETS1, MS-ETS1, HS-ETS1 (2013)

as_of: NGSS as published April 2013; Louisiana's own science standards (LSS Science, 2017) carry equivalent engineering-design expectations — verify against the adopting state's document
strength_note: touches: the track's blocks at this band practise the performance expectation's core activity (defining a problem, generating and comparing solutions, testing and improving). The mapping is at track-and-band level, authored by the maintainers, not a block-by-block alignment review. Use it to find the door, not to claim the room.
caveat: Verify each code against the current NGSS or state science document before classroom use. A code names an intended alignment, not a certification of it.

entries.why: Asking what a machine cannot reach and drawing how it moves is a simple problem defined and a solution sketched.
Criteria and constraints on a mechanism (reach, force, power) and comparing two ways to move a load.
Precision in defining a mechanism's problem and evaluating competing designs against criteria.
Quantified criteria for a real mechanism and breaking a motion problem into solvable parts.
Trade-offs between reach, force, cost and safety in a design the learner can measure.
Testing two ways to make a bot follow a line and saying which worked better.
Fair tests of a controller with one variable changed at a time.
Iterative tuning of something that oscillates; results used to improve the next version.
Evaluating a controller against criteria and using a model to predict its behaviour before running it.
Simulation-first evaluation of a plan meeting the world, with the model's limits stated.
Asking what a machine needs before it can do its job at a real place.
A site's constraints defined; a fair test of whether the machine meets them.
Site survey as problem definition; acceptance testing as evaluation against criteria.
Integration with what is already there broken into parts; commissioning as prioritized-criteria evaluation.
The gap list and the acceptance test are the engineering-design cycle closed on a real system.
Drawing what a machine is made of and which parts could be reused.
Comparing two designs for how easily they are repaired.
Evaluating designs for repair and energy use against criteria.
Trade-offs including environmental impact across a machine's life.
Prioritized criteria — cost, safety, reliability, environmental impact — for refurbishment against replacement.
